content:
As in the title. If you check any pull request, you'll see 1 check shown up as red (the reconcile one).

While it doesn't seem to affect functionality (?), it is annoying, and possibly deserve further scrutiny. If it's useless, probably a good idea to ignore it entirely to conserve resources.

Here's what Claude told me about it:

Almost every time, that check was cancelled on purpose, and gh pr checks (and GitHub's checks summary) count a cancelled check as a failure. The check is the reconcile job of TauCeti's "PR status" workflow, which keeps every PR's status label and Zulip post current. Every PR event (push, label, build finished, scoreboard posted) wakes it, but the job shares one repo-wide concurrency group, pr-status. GitHub runs one job at a time and keeps only the newest waiting one, cancelling the rest before they get a runner. One option: collapsed runs could report as skipped instead of cancelled, or the job could stop attaching a check to every PR. That would clear the red marks and the "unstable" state.
